**Finding: deviation (critical) — § 14.2, ¶ p0054**

Section 14.2 gives Cobalt exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created specifically for Juniper Ridge, with only a *revocable, non-transferable* licence lasting no longer than the Order Form term. That is the wrong direction on work we commission and pay for, and it fails the fallback as well as the preferred position — the fallback requires at minimum a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense; § 13.2's perpetual licence reaches only Vendor Technology, not the Deliverables.

The rest of the IP package is sound and needs no change:
- § 14.1 — Customer owns Customer Data, Confidential Information and independently developed IP; no transfer to Vendor.
- § 14.3 — Vendor retains Vendor Technology, but embedded Vendor Technology carries the § 13.2 perpetual/irrevocable/royalty-free licence, plus a pre-delivery disclosure duty.
- § 14.4 — no joint ownership absent a signed instrument; feedback rights are non-attributed and we keep unrestricted use.
- § 15.1 — no sale, ad use, data commingling or model training on Customer Data.

**Redline (validated, preferred level):** reverse the assignment in 14.2 to Customer with an express assignment on creation, while preserving Vendor's background IP and Vendor Technology by cross-reference to 14.3. The comment offers the licence-back fallback if Cobalt insists on retaining title.
